headline: Highest risk is medium: oh-my-openagent’s broad network/MCP hooks can amplify ComfyUI outputs into prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors, but ComfyUI itself is offline and write-limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can emit workflow/content artifacts, and oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks plus browser/network access, so a shared file or message bridge could let attacker-controlled content influence agent B. ComfyUI is offline by default, which lowers exposure, but B’s permissive tool surface makes instruction hijacking plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into oh-my-openagent prompts or watched files
IF runtime-injected MCPs or hooks parse ComfyUI-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Disable any file-watching or auto-ingest bridge between the tools
Require manual review before B consumes ComfyUI outputs
Restrict B to a non-browsing, no-MCP mode for shared workflows
Use separate workspaces for generated assets and agent prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all ComfyUI outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, seeds, checkpoints, and other model assets, while oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider auth data and can send data to external services. If they share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive model assets or auth-adjacent context can leak from A into B’s broader networked environment. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory tree
IF ComfyUI model assets or seeds are opened by oh-my-openagent
IF B forwards copied context to external APIs
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different OS users
Keep ComfyUI assets in a directory B cannot read
Disable B’s external API calls for shared sessions
Rotate any provider auth data used in B after shared work
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem write, git, or subprocess capability, while oh-my-openagent can spawn subprocesses and use broad network egress. That means there is little direct write-write conflict between the pair. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration that grants A additional write paths not present in its profile, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants ComfyUI write access not listed in its profile
IF both agents are configured to mutate the same mutable resource
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI read-only with respect to shared repos
Avoid concurrent edits to the same project tree
Run B without write access during ComfyUI sessions
Document ownership of any shared mutable resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can act on browser/networked information and has task-oriented hooks, so if it treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated artifacts into downstream actions. ComfyUI can produce workflows and assets, but it does not verify facts for B. The interaction is plausible in default agentic use, though not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as ground truth
IF B executes tasks or sends messages based on unverified ComfyUI output
mitigations: Require B to cite independent sources before acting
Insert a human approval step before any outbound action
Limit B to drafting only, not execution
Log provenance for every ComfyUI-derived claim
requires-engineering: add verification gates between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source. However, oh-my-openagent handles provider auth prompts and telemetry while ComfyUI can process local media assets, so a compliance issue could arise if regulated data is routed through B’s external services. Because the profiles do not show a concrete mismatch, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into oh-my-openagent
IF B’s external services retain or transmit that data beyond policy
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through B
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs only
Review telemetry settings before use
Keep ComfyUI assets local and offline
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
